title: Legislation and Regulation
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze the legislative process, statutory interpretation (text, canons, legislative history and purpose), agencies and delegation, rulemaking and adjudication under the Administrative Procedure Act, and judicial review of agency interpretations after Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (2024).

weeks.10: Skidmore weight and the major questions doctrine

blocks.deliverable: Interpret a supplied statute by its text alone.
Apply five canons to an ambiguous provision.
Trace a rule from proposal to final rule.
Week 7 midterm; decide whether an agency rule is arbitrary and capricious.
Explain how a court now reviews an agency's reading of a statute.
Redraft an ambiguous provision to remove the ambiguity.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Statutory interpretation memo: for a supplied statute and agency rule written for the course, write a 2,000-word memo arguing both readings and predicting how a court would rule.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
